Fixes sign error in flux divergence of `AnisotropicBiharmonicDiffusivity` (#1703)

* Fixes sign error in flux divergence of biharmonic stress and diffusive flux

Resolves #1702 noticed by @mukund-gupta .

In a previous PR we changed the notation of the closure term to indicate that it's the divergence of a flux, rather than specifically the divergence of a _viscous_ or _diffusive_ flux. This notational change required us to change the term's sign. However, we did not change the sign of the flux divergence for `AnisotropicBiharmonicDiffusivity`; we only changed the _name_ of the term.

This PR fixes that.

Change default output array type for `JLD2OutputWriter` to `Array{Float64}` (#2890)

* Change default output array type for `JLD2OutputWriter` to Array{Float64}

While `Array{Float32}` is neat because user output is smaller, it's a bad default because it often leads to confusing results, like the fact that outputing `Field(Integral(c))` is different (possibly by `eps(Float32)`) than computing `Integral(c_output)` in post processing.

Thus @xkykai and I propose to make the default `Array{Float64}`. We could regard outputting with `Array{Float32}` as an "optimization" which is premature as a default.

Introduce Abstract formulation types for FourierTridiagonalPoissonSolver (#4936)

* Introduce Abstract formulation types for FourierTridiagonalPoissonSolver

The formulation does two things:

1. it controls how the diagonals are computed and
2. it determines whether or not to apply the zero-mean gauge condition

We need to be able to modulate these independently for variations on the Poisson problem; eg problems like those encountered in an anelastic pressure correction algorithm (which modifies the z-dependent term and thus the diagonals, but is still a homogeneous problem with a gauge condition).

Support FFT planning for `ConcreteRArray` (#5246)

* Add AbstractFFTs to weakdeps and compat

Add AbstractFFTs as a weak dependency in Project.toml, include it in OceananigansReactantExt, and set a compatibility bound (AbstractFFTs = "1.5"). This ensures the Reactant extension has access to FFT functionality and declares the minimum compatible AbstractFFTs version.

* Add Reactant FFT plans and related tests

Introduce Solvers.jl to provide Reactant-aware FFT plan types and plan_forward_transform/plan_backward_transform methods (Periodic -> FFT, Flat -> no-op, Bounded -> explicit error). Wire Solvers into OceananigansReactantExt.jl. Update Utils.jl to import heuristic_workgroup and add commented Reactant-specific workgroup heuristics. Add test harness and investigation tests: test/Project.toml with Reactant and PJRT preference, fft-ad tests (compilation and AD investigation), and a comprehensive reactant correctness test suite. These changes enable FFT usage with Reactant arrays and add tests to validate compilation/AD and runtime correctness.

* Use ReactantAbstractFFTsExt FFT plans

Replace custom Reactant FFT plan structs and Application with extension-provided plans. Solvers.jl now gets ReactantAbstractFFTsExt via Base.get_extension(Reactant, :ReactantAbstractFFTsExt) and returns ReactantFFTInPlacePlan/ReactantIFFTInPlacePlan parametrized by element type instead of defining local plan structs or using AbstractFFTs. Minor wording tweaks to Bounded topology errors and added section comments. Utils.jl: remove unused import of heuristic_workgroup (keep prettytime and prettysummary).

* Add FFTW+Reactant MWE and bump Reactant dep

(0.105.1) Add density and gravity_wave_speed to PerturbationAdvection (#5314)

* Add density and gravity_wave_speed to PerturbationAdvection

Extends PerturbationAdvection with two optional features needed for
models with density-weighted prognostic variables (e.g., anelastic models):

1. `density` field: when provided, converts density-weighted fields (ρψ)
   to intensive fields (ψ) before radiation and back after. This fixes the
   dimensional inconsistency when applying PerturbationAdvection directly
   to prognostic variables like ρu, ρθ, ρq.

2. `gravity_wave_speed`: additional phase speed added to the advective
   velocity, following Klemp & Wilhelmson (1978). Useful for momentum
   fields where gravity waves propagate faster than the mean flow.

Both default to `nothing` and `0` respectively, so this is fully backward
compatible — existing code using PerturbationAdvection is unaffected.

Also adds _fill_*_halo! methods for Center-located fields, enabling
PerturbationAdvection to be used on scalar fields (tracers, ρθ, etc.)
in addition to Face-located velocity/momentum fields.

Motivated by NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#494 which currently maintains a
separate PerturbationMomentumAdvection scheme with ~270 lines of
duplicated radiation logic.

this triggers "Attempt to donate a buffer which is also used by the

via Δt + zero(Δt) for last_stage_Δt.

Fix Float32 WENO smoothness indicators via constant shift (#5491)

* Mean-subtract WENO stencils to fix Float32 smoothness indicators

The smoothness indicator β is a quadratic form ψᵀCψ that is invariant
to constant shifts (it measures derivatives of the interpolating
polynomial). In Float32, when stencil values have a large mean
(e.g., ρθ ≈ 300), the quadratic form suffers catastrophic cancellation:
terms of O(ψ²) ≈ O(10⁵) cancel to give β ≈ O(10⁻²), exceeding
Float32's ~7 significant digits. This produces negative β values and
wildly incorrect WENO weights.

The fix subtracts the stencil mean before computing β, reducing operand
magnitudes from O(ψ) to O(Δψ). This eliminates cancellation and
recovers Float64-accurate results (relative error < 0.001%) at a cost
of ~11 FLOPs per sub-stencil. A dispatch on NTuple{N, Float32} ensures
zero overhead for Float64.

Closes CliMA/Oceananigans.jl#5485

Size BatchedTridiagonalSolver scratch by worksize, fixing OOB on RightFaceFolded tripolar grids (#5594)

* Size BatchedTridiagonalSolver scratch by worksize, not (Nx, Ny, Nz)

On grids whose `worksize` exceeds the interior size in any dimension —
notably `RightFaceFolded` tripolar grids whose `Utils.worksize` is
`(Nx, Ny+1, Nz)` — the previous (Nx, Ny, Nz) scratch lets the tridiagonal
kernel write `t[i, Ny+1, k]` out of bounds. Under Julia's column-major
layout this byte aliases `t[i, 1, k+1]`, corrupting the j=1 column's
back-substitution slot. On a sequential CPU launch the columns are
processed end-to-end so the OOB write never races with the j=1 read;
on a parallel GPU launch they race, producing a deterministic
contamination at the first interior row of the rank whose j=Ny+1
holds the most divergent value — i.e. the northernmost rank of a 1xN
distributed tripolar partition, where j=Ny+1 holds the fold halo κ
rather than a smooth neighbour-rank κ.

For non-RFTRG grids `worksize(grid) == size(grid)` so this is a no-op.

Add ZarrWriter and FieldTimeSeries Zarr reader (#5605)

* Add ZarrWriter and FieldTimeSeries Zarr reader

Implements `ZarrWriter` as a new output writer backed by Zarr.jl, alongside
JLD2Writer and NetCDFWriter. Lives in an extension that triggers on `using Zarr`.

Closes #3821.

## Layout

Lean-chunked, non-CF: each output is a chunked Zarr array of shape
`(spatial..., Nt)` growing along the time axis. `_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS` set to
`trilocation_dim_name`-style names (reversed for C-order). Grid reconstruction
serialized as JSON in a `grid/` (or `grid_<n>/` for multi-grid) subgroup.
CF compliance left additive for a follow-up.

## Features

- Inputs: `AbstractField`, `AbstractOperation`, `Reduction`, `WindowedTimeAverage`,
  functions (with `dimensions` kwarg). Same surface as `JLD2Writer`.
- Multi-grid support via unique-grid detection + per-output `grid_index` attr.
- File splitting (`NoFileSplitting` / `FileSizeLimit` / `TimeInterval`).
- Append-on-existing-store with dtype validation on restart.
- Compression via user-supplied `compressor` kwarg (default `NoCompressor`).
- Stores: `DirectoryStore` (default), `DictStore` (memory), `S3Store`. `ZipStore`
  rejected on write with a clear error pointing at `Zarr.writezip` for the
  finalize-to-zip workflow.
- `FieldTimeSeries(path, name)` reader: auto-detects `.zarr` and `.zip`.
- MPI distributed writes: per-axis GCD chunk default, rank-0-owned metadata
  + time writes, lock-free per-rank chunk-aligned data writes,
  rank-topology in `.zattrs` for restart validation. Particles rejected
  under MPI in v1.

## Tests

- `test/test_zarr_writer.jl` — 108 serial tests across 7 testsets covering API
  surface, raw round-trip, operations/reductions/functions/WindowedTimeAverage,
  grid reconstruction + multi-grid, FieldTimeSeries reader, append + dtype
  validation on restart, DictStore + ZipStore-read.
- `test/test_distributed_zarr_writer.jl` + `test/distributed_zarr_writer_tests.jl`
  — `mpiexec`-driven driver exercising Partition(x=2), Partition(y=2),
  Partition(x=2, y=2); 15 passing tests.
- `test/manual/test_zarr_s3.jl` — env-gated S3/MinIO smoke test (not in CI).

## Benchmarks

Comparative scripts in `benchmark/zarr_writer/` (not part of CI) for running
ZarrWriter vs JLD2Writer vs NetCDFWriter on CPU.

## Plan

`zarr_writer_plan.md` documents the locked-in design decisions, on-disk layout,
prior-art comparison (SpeedyWeather), forward-compatibility path to CF, and
implementation-phase status.

* Restrict ZarrExt's Field method dispatch to Zarr.ZArray

The reader's `Field(loc::Tuple, arr, name::String, time_index::Int; ...)` had
`arr::Any`, which created a method ambiguity with the existing JLD2 method
`Field(location, file::JLD2.JLDFile, name::String, iter; ...)`:
  - `Field(loc::Tuple, arr::Any, ...)` is more specific on arg 1
  - `Field(location::Any, file::JLD2.JLDFile, ...)` is more specific on arg 2
Neither subsumes the other, so calls like `Field(loc, jldfile, name, iter)`
inside `set_from_jld2!` dispatched into the Zarr extension's method by chance
of ambiguity resolution, hit `ndims(jldfile)` and errored.

Restricting `arr::Zarr.ZArray` resolves the ambiguity: the Zarr method matches
only when both args 1 and 2 are right; the JLD2 method matches only when arg 2
is a JLDFile.

Fixes the `cpu/gpu-simulation-tests` and OutputReaders errors (19 errored
tests locally; reproduced.)

Fix `set!(::DistributedField, ::Field)` regression from #5586 (#5619)

#5586 routed `set_to_field!` through `on_architecture(child_architecture(u), v)`
+ `fill_halo_regions!(v_on_u)` + `interpolate!` whenever
`matching_field_discretization` is false. On distributed fields that path is
broken in two ways:

1. `indices(u) == indices(v)` rejects equivalent windows like `(:, :, :)` vs
   `(1:Nx, 1:Ny, 1:Nz)`, sending well-formed `set!` calls down the else
   branch unnecessarily. `TransposableField` constructs zfield/yfield/xfield
   with explicit unit-range indices, so `set!(Φ.zfield, ϕ)` in
   `test_distributed_transpose.jl` always falls through.

2. `on_architecture(child_architecture(u), v)` strips `Distributed{CPU}` to
   `CPU` on the grid but leaves the `DistributedCommunicationBoundaryCondition`s
   (and the precompiled `DistributedFillHalo` kernels) intact. The subsequent
   `fill_halo_regions!(v_on_u)` then dispatches to the non-distributed path
   and invokes `DistributedFillHalo{WestAndEast}` with 6 args via the inlined
   `fill_halo_event!`, when the only method takes 7 (`c, bc1, bc2, loc, grid,
   arch, buffers`) — MethodError.

Fixes:

* `matching_field_discretization` now treats `Colon` and the equivalent full
  `UnitRange` as the same window (per-dimension, parameterized by size). Same
  size + same location + equivalent windows now correctly takes the cheap
  copy path.

* `set_to_field!` fills halos on `v`'s native architecture before migrating,
  so distributed dispatch is used when `v` is distributed. The post-migration
  `interpolate!` then samples a field whose halos are already populated.

Repros via `test/test_distributed_transpose.jl` (passed at parent of #5586,
failed at the merge of #5586).

* Fix _fractional_indices arity dispatch for reduced-source set!

`set!(::Field, ::Field)` routes to `interpolate!` when sizes or locations
don't match (introduced in #5586). For a destination at (Center,Center,Center)
on a (Bounded,Flat,Bounded) grid and a reduced source at (Nothing,Nothing,Center),
the kernel passes `flatten_node`'s 2-tuple `(x, z)` into
`_fractional_indices(at, grid, nothing, nothing, ℓz)`.

The intended method here is the 1-tuple `(z,)` version (which would recurse
correctly), but Julia's function-arg destructuring is permissive: the pattern
`(z,)` happily binds to the first element of a longer tuple. So the dispatcher
picked the 1-tuple branch and ran `fractional_z_index(x_value, ...)`, producing
a kk far outside the source's z range. The resulting interior wrote garbage
memory (and NaN past the end), which then poisoned every downstream
`set!(model; ρ=ref.density)` and triggered `DomainError` in any subsequent
`θ^γ` in compressible thermodynamics.

Two-part fix:
- Add explicit `::NTuple{1, Any}` / `::NTuple{2, Any}` / `::NTuple{3, Any}`
  constraints to every `_fractional_indices` method so the dispatcher cannot
  silently bind a longer tuple to a shorter pattern.
- Add three 2-tuple "pruning" methods for the cases where the source has more
  `Nothing` locations than the destination has `Flat` dims — they mirror the
  3-tuple recursive prunes at lines 228/231/234 but for the case where
  `to_grid`'s `flatten_node` already produced a 2-tuple.

Add NCCL extension and implement NCCLFourierTridiagonalPoissonSolver (#5445)

* Skip fill_corners! when no corner neighbors exist

Avoid calling `sync_device!` (CUDA.synchronize) in `fill_corners!` when
all corner connectivity is `nothing`. This occurs for slab decompositions
and single-rank distributed configurations where no diagonal neighbors exist.

Each `sync_device!` call flushes the GPU's async execution pipeline. With
~300 halo fills per 10 timesteps in a typical Breeze.jl anelastic benchmark,
the unnecessary syncs cause a 2.95x overhead on a single distributed GPU.
This fix reduces the overhead to 1.19x.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Eliminate permutedims for Periodic y-FFT in distributed solver

For doubly-periodic grids on GPU, plan the y-FFT along dimension 2
directly instead of reshaping to (Ny, Nx, Nz) and planning along
dimension 1. This eliminates two permutedims! calls per y-FFT, which
were the dominant cost in the distributed solver (69% of solve time).

The old approach was: reshape → plan on dim 1 → permutedims → FFT → permutedims
The new approach is: plan on dim 2 → FFT (cuFFT handles strided access natively)

For Bounded y-topology, the old reshape approach is preserved because
twiddle factors and index permutations assume a dim-1 layout.

Also skip y-buffer allocation for Periodic y (no index permutation needed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Optimize Z-stretched solve for slab-x: 4→2 MPI transposes

For slab-x decomposition (Ry=1), the z-direction is always fully local
in x-local space. This means the tridiagonal solve can be performed
directly after the forward FFTs in x-local space, without transposing
back to z-local space first.

The optimized algorithm:
  y-FFT → transpose_y_to_x(MPI) → x-FFT → tridiag_solve → x-IFFT → transpose_x_to_y(MPI) → y-IFFT

instead of the general algorithm:
  y-FFT → transpose_y_to_x(MPI) → x-FFT → transpose_x_to_y(MPI) → tridiag_solve → transpose_y_to_x(MPI) → x-IFFT → transpose_x_to_y(MPI) → y-IFFT

This halves the number of MPI all-to-all operations per pressure solve
from 4 to 2, reducing both communication volume and pipeline stalls
from GPU synchronization.

The tridiagonal solver is set up on the x-local grid with correctly
partitioned eigenvalues. The general pencil decomposition path is
preserved for Ry > 1.

* Fix NCCL communicator finalizer deadlock with multiple communicators per process

NCCL.Communicator installs a finalizer that calls ncclCommDestroy, a blocking
collective. Julia's GC runs at uncoordinated times across MPI ranks, so when a
communicator becomes garbage, GC on one rank can fire ncclCommDestroy while the
other ranks are inside an unrelated NCCL collective (ncclCommInitRank while
creating another communicator, or a SendRecv during a halo fill) — deadlocking
the job.

A normal simulation creates a single long-lived communicator and never hits
this. It bites code that creates several communicators in one process — e.g. the
NCCL extension test suite, which sweeps (4,1,1)/(1,4,1)/(2,2,1) decompositions
across the halo-correctness, transpose, and Poisson testsets. The deadlock
reproduced reliably on the 3rd communicator-with-exchanges (one rank blocked in
futex, the others spinning, GPUs idle).

Fix: root every NCCL communicator we create in a module-level registry so its
finalizer never runs at an uncoordinated point (released together at process
teardown), and disable GC across the collective creation as defense-in-depth.

Verified on 4x A100: a 4-communicator create+fill repro now completes with GC
enabled, and the full neighbor-value halo-correctness testset passes 15/15
(edges, corners, both Z topologies, multi-field, halo 2/4, X/Y/ZFaceField, async).

* Let Reactant `set!(u, v)` broadcast reduced fields instead of hopping to the CPU

Since #5586, `set_to_field!(::ReactantField, ::ReactantField)` takes the
CPU interpolation fallback whenever sizes or locations differ, including
for a reduced column field (e.g. a 1D reference profile) being set into
a full 3D field. Under Reactant tracing that fallback cannot work: its
first step, `on_architecture(CPU(), grid)`, rebuilds the traced grid
through the validating constructor, and validate_lat_lon_grid_args then
drives `||` with a `TracedRNumber{Bool}`:

    TypeError: non-boolean (Reactant.TracedRNumber{Bool}) used in boolean context

(and even past validation, traced data cannot be materialized on the CPU
mid-trace). Before #5586 this case was handled by the extension's plain
`interior(u) .= interior(v)` broadcast, which traces fine.

Restore that behavior by widening the fast path: a dimension may be
copied by broadcasting when both fields share its location and size, or
when v is reduced there (Nothing location, singleton size). The strict
old condition is a subset, so other cases are unchanged.

This fixes Breeze.jl's Reactant lat-lon compilation tests, broken since
its reference states became column fields set into 3D density fields
inside compiled functions (NumericalEarth/Breeze.jl#863).

Name the copy-versus-interpolate cases and share them with Reactant (#5878)

`set!(u, v)` decides whether to copy or interpolate, and the Reactant extension
had its own copy of that decision. The two drifted: #5652 taught the base
predicate that a degenerate dimension may be copied whichever side is reduced,
while the extension's `broadcast_compatible` (added later, in #5840) only
accepted a reduced *source*. Setting a `Field{Center, Center, Nothing}` from a
windowed single layer therefore missed the extension's copy path and fell to its
CPU interpolation fallback, which throws inside `@compile`/`@jit`.

Replace both predicates with one, decomposed into the three situations under
which a dimension may be copied, each named:

  equivalent_dimension         same location, extent, and window
  degenerate_dimension         both span one point, at least one carries no node
  expandable_source_dimension  v carries no node and stretches across u

`matching_field_discretization` becomes `copyable_fields` and
`matching_field_dimension` becomes `copyable_dimension`, since what callers
branch on is whether a copy is valid, not whether discretizations coincide --- a
one-cell column and an eight-cell field do not share a discretization, yet
copying by expansion is exactly right.

Expansion is new to the base predicate. It was previously routed to
`interpolate!`, and broadcast expansion is bit-identical to that result wherever
the source carries no node, so this only skips a kernel. `copy_to_field!` now
takes that path explicitly rather than reaching it through the `try`/`catch`
interior fallback.

The Reactant extension keeps only mechanism: it copies interiors rather than
attempting halos through a `try`/`catch` that cannot be traced, and retains the
CPU `interpolate!` fallback for genuine interpolation. No policy remains in the
extension, so base fixes now reach Reactant automatically.

Also fixes a silent bug in the extension's predicate: it never received field
indices, so two same-size, same-location fields windowed at different levels
compared equal and were copied raw, where base interpolates by physical
position.

Read Field boundary conditions windowed to a plane at their own plane (#5881)

* Read Field boundary conditions windowed to a plane at their own plane

An array-valued boundary condition is evaluated as `condition[i, j, 1]`, which is
right for a plain 2D array and for a `Field` reduced along the boundary-normal
direction, but not for a `Field` windowed to a boundary plane with `indices`,
e.g. `GradientBoundaryCondition(Field(-g * ρ, indices = (:, :, grid.Nz)))`:
such a field stores its data offset to the window (its k-axis is `Nz:Nz`), so
`[i, j, 1]` silently reads out of bounds under `@inbounds` (and throws a
`BoundsError` with `--check-bounds=yes`). Nothing validated array-valued
conditions either.

Fields windowed to a single plane in one direction are now read at their own
plane, in `getbc` methods dispatching on the `Field`'s indices type parameter,
for the x, y and z boundaries. Their location and window are preserved when
they are adapted for kernels, as is already done for reduced fields, so that
these methods also dispatch on the GPU. `regularize_boundary_condition` now
rejects a `Field` windowed to more than one plane, or windowed along a
tangential direction, with an `ArgumentError`. Reduced fields and plain arrays
behave as before.

(0.111.0) Complete implicit advection implementation by including `ZFaceField`s treatment (#5903)

* Dispatch implicit vertical advection coefficients on the field's z-location

The adaptive-implicit get_coefficient methods did not dispatch on the
advected field's vertical location, so the implicit solve for w in a
NonhydrostaticModel with adaptive-implicit momentum advection applied
z-Center tracer coefficients to a z-Face field — inconsistent with the
Ww flux, which is deliberately kept fully explicit. They also required
downstream extensions of get_coefficient to track its exact trailing
arity: when the arity changed, typed extensions silently fell through
to the diffusion-only catch-alls instead of erroring.

Thread the field's ℓz through implicit_advection_upper/lower/diagonal
and make those functions the single dispatch point for the advection
contribution:

- explicit schemes and advection = nothing contribute zero at any
  location;
- adaptive-implicit schemes return the existing coefficients at
  ℓz::Center and zero at ℓz::Face, consistent with the fully explicit
  Ww flux;
- any other advection type raises a MethodError, so downstream models
  (e.g. mass-flux models solving vertical momentum implicitly) extend
  these three functions — dispatching on their own advection type
  and/or ℓz — instead of get_coefficient, and a mismatch fails loudly
  instead of silently dropping the advection contribution.

The get_coefficient methods for the vertically-implicit diffusion
solver collapse to three untyped forwarders, removing the AIVA-typed
duplicates and the silent catch-alls.

Add a regression test for the z-Face behavior, including a
NonhydrostaticModel time step with adaptive-implicit momentum
advection, which exercises the implicit step of w.

* Post halo MPI requests into preallocated slots

Each field's `CommState` now owns one `MPI.UnsafeMultiRequest` with a send and a
receive slot per side, laid out so that every exchange (west + east, south + north,
corners) uses a contiguous range of slots. The `DistributedFillHalo` kernels post into
their slots and return the slot range instead of allocating a `Vector{MPI.Request}`.

`progress_comms!` calls `MPI_Testall` directly on that range with a per-exchange flag
stored in the state, so polling no longer allocates (`MPI.Testall` allocates its flag
at every call). `waitall_comms!` completes a range for the synchronous paths, and
`wait_for_comms!` completes all slots, which replaces `pending_requests` for
single-threaded runs.

On the 360x180x50 tripolar benchmark (2 ranks, GPU, 4 threads) this removes ~27% of the
allocations per time step on the rank that waits longest, at unchanged step time.

Move LatitudeLongitudeGrid vertical coordinates to ReactantState via Adapt (#6007)

* Move LatitudeLongitudeGrid vertical coordinates to ReactantState via Adapt

`on_architecture(::ReactantState, ::LatitudeLongitudeGrid)` rebuilds the grid
field by field through `_to_reactant`, which had one hand-written method per
type and knew only `StaticVerticalDiscretization`. Any other vertical
coordinate (`MutableVerticalDiscretization`, or one defined downstream such as
a terrain-following coordinate) hit a MethodError.

Replace the hand-written methods with an Adapt adaptor: `Adapt.adapt` recurses
through every struct that defines `adapt_structure`, which all GPU-capable
coordinates already do, materializing arrays and ranges into ConcreteRArrays
and passing numbers through. Results are identical to the previous helper on
static-coordinate grids.
